extracted.intended_audience: district court judges, patent litigators, and court clerks managing patent cases
extracted.subtask_description: Model scheduling order and protective-order standards for managing patent litigation in U.S. district courts, including disclosure deadlines, discovery limits, briefing/page limits, claim construction procedures, tutorials, and confidentiality/source-code protections. Provides procedural requirements and substantive definitions to guide parties and the Court through early case management, discovery disputes, pretrial, trial, and post-trial stages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Papers Filed Under Seal
rubrics_metrics.description: A redacted version of any sealed document shall be filed electronically within seven (7) days of the filing of the sealed document. If a party intends to request sealing or redaction of any portion of a transcript, the party should note that intent at the start of the proceeding and, promptly after completion of the transcript, file a motion for sealing/redaction attaching (1) a copy of the complete transcript highlighted to identify text proposed to be sealed/redacted and (2) a copy of the proposed redacted/sealed transcript.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The party seeking redactions must demonstrate why there is good cause for the redactions and why disclosure would work a clearly defined and serious injury to the party seeking redaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Courtesy Copies Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Except for discovery matters governed elsewhere and the final pretrial order, parties shall provide to the Court two (2) courtesy copies of all briefs and one (1) courtesy copy of any other document filed in support of any briefs (appendices, exhibits, declarations, affidavits, etc.).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This requirement also applies to papers filed under seal.

rubrics_metrics.name: ADR Referral
rubrics_metrics.description: This matter is referred to a magistrate judge to explore the possibility of alternative dispute resolution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Plaintiff Disclosure — Identification of Accused Products and Patents
rubrics_metrics.description: Plaintiff shall identify the accused product(s), including accused methods and systems, and its damages model, as well as the asserted patent(s) that the accused product(s) allegedly infringe(s). Plaintiff shall also produce the file history for each asserted patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deadline placeholders provided in order; disclosure is subject to agreement among the parties and Court approval.

rubrics_metrics.name: Defendant Disclosure — Core Technical Documents and Sales Figures
rubrics_metrics.description: Defendant shall produce core technical documents related to the accused product(s), sufficient to show how the accused product(s) work(s), including but not limited to non-publicly available operation manuals, product literature, schematics, and specifications. Defendant shall also produce sales figures for the accused product(s).

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial Claim Chart (Plaintiff)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plaintiff shall produce an initial claim chart relating each known accused product to the asserted claims each such product allegedly infringes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial Invalidity Contentions (Defendant)
rubrics_metrics.description: Defendant shall produce its initial invalidity contentions for each asserted claim, as well as the known related invalidating references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Infringement and Invalidity Contentions
rubrics_metrics.description: Plaintiff shall provide final infringement contentions by a set date; Defendant shall provide final invalidity contentions by a set date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deadlines to be set in scheduling order; supplementation obligations discussed elsewhere in the Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Observe Local Rule 26.1 Discovery Limitations
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise ordered by the Court, the limitations on discovery set forth in Local Rule 26.1 shall be strictly observed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovery Cut-Off Deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: All discovery in this case shall be initiated so that it will be completed on or before the court's discovery cut-off date.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Date to be inserted in the scheduling order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Document Production Substantial Completion
rubrics_metrics.description: Document production shall be substantially complete by the date set in the scheduling order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Date to be provided in each case-specific scheduling order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requests for Admission Limit
rubrics_metrics.description: A maximum of ____ requests for admission are permitted for each side.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The blank is to be filled in per-case; parties must adhere to the limit unless the Court permits otherwise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interrogatories Limits and Contention Interrogatory Guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: A maximum number of interrogatories, including contention interrogatories, are permitted for each side. The Court encourages parties to serve and respond to contention interrogatories early in the case. In the absence of agreement, contention interrogatories should first be addressed by the party with the burden of proof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The adequacy of interrogatory answers shall be judged by the level of detail each party provides; more detail provided justifies more detail received.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deposition Hours Limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Each side is limited to a total of _ hours of taking testimony by deposition upon oral examination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Blank to be filled in per case; parties must track and observe total hours limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deposition Location Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Any party or representative (officer, director, or managing agent) of a party filing a civil action in this district court must ordinarily be required, upon request, to submit to a deposition at a place designated within this district.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions may be made by order of the Court. A defendant who becomes a counterclaimant/cross-claimant/third-party plaintiff is considered to have filed an action for purpose of this provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert Testimony Disclosure Deadlines and Limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial Federal Rule 26(a)(2) disclosure of expert testimony for the party with the initial burden is due by a date set in the scheduling order; supplemental disclosures to contradict or rebut are due by another date; reply expert reports from the party with the initial burden are due by another date. No other expert reports will be permitted without consent of all parties or leave of Court. Parties shall advise dates/times of their experts' availability for deposition along with reports.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deadlines and whether expert declarations may be filed in connection with motions briefing are to be chosen by parties (permitted or not).

rubrics_metrics.name: Expert Declaration/In-Brief Expert Submission Choice
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties must elect whether they will or will not permit expert declarations to be filed in connection with motions briefing (including case-dispositive motions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The scheduling order requires the parties to choose one of the options: [will] [will not].

rubrics_metrics.name: Daubert Objections Timing and Briefing
rubrics_metrics.description: Objections to expert testimony made pursuant to Daubert/Fed. R. Evid. 702 must be made by motion no later than the deadline for dispositive motions set forth in the scheduling order, unless otherwise ordered by the Court. Briefing on such motions is subject to the page limits set out for case dispositive motions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Daubert motions are consolidated into the overall case-dispositive motion schedule and page limits (see combined page limits).

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovery Dispute Procedures — Meet and Confer Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Any discovery motion filed without first complying with the required procedures (good faith efforts including verbal communication among Delaware and Lead Counsel) will be denied without prejudice to renew pursuant to these procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Counsel must include at least one Delaware Counsel and at least one Lead Counsel per party in meet-and-confer efforts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discovery Dispute — Joint Letter and Teleconference Process
rubrics_metrics.description: If parties cannot resolve a discovery matter, they shall submit a joint letter requesting scheduling of a discovery teleconference and must list the disputes requiring judicial attention in a non-argumentative manner. The filing party shall file a 3-page letter outlining issues and position generally not less than 48 hours prior to the conference; opposing party may file a 3-page response not less than 24 hours prior.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each party shall submit two courtesy copies of its discovery letter and attachments. The Court may require further briefing or resolve disputes prior to teleconference and cancel the conference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motions to Amend — Letter Format and Attachments
rubrics_metrics.description: Any motion to amend shall NOT be accompanied by an opening brief but shall instead be accompanied by a letter, not to exceed three (3) pages, describing the basis for the requested relief, and shall attach the proposed amended pleading and a 'blackline' comparison to the prior pleading.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opposing party has seven (7) days to file a responsive letter (≤5 pages). The moving party may file a reply letter (≤2 pages) within three (3) days and request a teleconference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motions to Strike — Letter Format and Timing
rubrics_metrics.description: Any motion to strike shall NOT be accompanied by an opening brief but shall instead be accompanied by a letter, not to exceed three (3) pages, describing the basis for the requested relief, and shall attach the document to be stricken.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opposition due within seven (7) days (≤5 pages); reply ≤2 pages within three (3) days; parties shall file a letter requesting a teleconference to address the motion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tutorial on Technology — Timing, Length, and Content
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties shall provide the Court, no later than the date on which their opening claim construction briefs are due, a tutorial on the technology at issue. The parties may separately or jointly submit a DVD of not more than thirty (30) minutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The tutorial should focus on the technology in issue and should not be used for argument. Parties may file tutorials under seal and each party may comment in writing (≤5 pages) on the opposing party’s tutorial. Parties should confirm Court's technical ability to access formats (best are 'mpeg' or 'quicktime').

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim Construction Issue Identification and Joint Chart
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties shall exchange a list of claim term(s)/phrase(s) they believe need construction and their proposed constructions. Parties will meet and confer to prepare a Joint Claim Construction Chart identifying disputed claim terms and each party’s proposed construction with citation(s) only to intrinsic evidence. A copy of the patent(s) and portions of the intrinsic record relied upon shall be submitted. This document will not be filed and shall not provide argument.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Joint Chart is intended to present intrinsic-evidence-only positions without argument; timelines for exchange and submission are set in the scheduling order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim Construction Briefing Sequence and Page Limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Parties shall contemporaneously submit initial briefs on claim construction issues and contemporaneously submit answering/responsive briefs. No reply briefs or supplemental papers on claim construction shall be submitted without leave of the Court. Local Rule 7.1.3(4) controls page limitations for initial and responsive briefs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Filing dates for briefs are set in the scheduling order; adhere to local rule page limits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearing on Claim Construction — Notice and Time Allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to the claim construction hearing parties shall notify the Court, by joint letter, whether they request leave to present testimony at the hearing and the amount of time they request to be allocated for the hearing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Court aims to issue its claim construction order within sixty (60) days of the conclusion of the hearing; it will advise the parties if unable to meet this goal.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim Status Report
rubrics_metrics.description: Counsel shall submit a joint letter to the Court with an interim report on the nature of the matters in issue and the progress of discovery to date on a set date. The Court may schedule a status conference if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Final Supplementation Requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Absent agreement among the parties and approval of the Court, parties must finally supplement, by a date set in the scheduling order, the identification of all accused products and of all invalidity references.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties should treat supplementation obligations seriously and conform to the deadline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case Dispositive Motions — Deadlines and Restrictions
rubrics_metrics.description: All case dispositive motions, opening briefs, and supporting affidavits shall be served and filed on or before the date set. No case dispositive motion under Rule 56 may be filed more than ten (10) days before that date without leave of the Court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Briefing is presented pursuant to Local Rules as modified by the Order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Combined Page Limits for Case Dispositive and Daubert Motions
rubrics_metrics.description: Each SIDE will be limited to a combined total of 40 pages for all opening briefs, 40 pages for all answering briefs, and 20 pages for all reply briefs regardless of the number of case dispositive motions filed. If a Daubert motion is filed in addition, the totals shall be increased to 50 pages for opening briefs, 50 pages for answering briefs, and 25 pages for reply briefs for each SIDE.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The parties must work together to ensure the Court receives no more than a total of 250 pages of briefing on all case dispositive and Daubert motions across consolidated/related cases (i.e., 50+50+25 per side times two sides = 250).

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearing Allocation for Dispositive and Daubert Motions
rubrics_metrics.description: The Court will hear argument on all pending case dispositive and Daubert motions on a scheduled date. Subject to further order, each side will be allocated a total of forty-five (45) minutes to present its argument on all pending motions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties should propose a hearing date approximately two months prior to the requested pretrial conference date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications by Motion — Filing and Local Rule Statement
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as specified, any application to the Court shall be by written motion filed with the Clerk. Any non-dispositive motion should contain the statement required by Local Rule 7.1.1.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pretrial Conference and Final Pretrial Order Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: The Court will hold a pretrial conference. Unless otherwise ordered, filing the pretrial order satisfies the pretrial disclosure requirement of Fed. R. Civ. P. 26(a)(3). Parties shall file the joint proposed final pretrial order with the information required by the form of Revised Final Pretrial Order- Patent by a date at least seven (7) days before the requested pretrial conference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The joint proposed final pretrial order shall include, among other things: (a) a request for a specific number of hours/days for trial presentations based on typical trial day hours; (b) position on objections to impeachment with prior testimony; (c) position on whether the Court should rule at trial on objections to expert testimony beyond prior disclosures or defer ruling; (d) position on how to make JMOL motions and whether they may be supplemented in writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Motions in Limine — Inclusion in Pretrial Order and Limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Motions in limine shall not be separately filed. All in limine requests and responses shall be set forth in the proposed pretrial order. Each SIDE is limited to three (3) in limine requests, unless otherwise permitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each in limine request may be supported by a maximum of three (3) pages of argument and opposed by a maximum of three (3) pages; the moving side may add one (1) additional page in reply. If multiple parties support or oppose, submissions shall be combined into a single three-page submission (and single one-page reply) unless otherwise ordered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Jury Instructions, Voir Dire, and Special Verdict Forms — Filing Format and Timing
rubrics_metrics.description: For jury trials, parties should file proposed voir dire, preliminary jury instructions, final jury instructions, and special verdict forms three (3) business days before the final pretrial conference.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This submission shall be accompanied by a courtesy copy containing electronic files of these documents in WordPerfect or Microsoft Word format, which may be submitted by e-mail to the judge’s staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trial Scheduling and Time Allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Trial scheduled for a set number of days beginning at 9:30 a.m. on the scheduled date, with subsequent days beginning at 9:00 a.m. Jury excused each day at 4:30 p.m. until deliberations. The trial will be timed; counsel will be allocated a total number of hours to present their cases.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties should request specific number of trial hours/days in the final pretrial order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judgment on Verdict and Post-Trial Status Report Deadline
rubrics_metrics.description: Within seven (7) days after a jury returns a verdict in any portion of a jury trial, the parties shall jointly submit a form of order to enter judgment on the verdict and submit a joint status report indicating how the case should proceed and listing any post-trial motions each party intends to file.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-Trial Motions Page Limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless otherwise ordered, all SIDES are limited to a maximum of 20 pages of opening briefs, 20 pages of answering briefs, and 10 pages of reply briefs relating to any post-trial motions filed by that side, no matter how many such motions are filed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and Limitations of Protective Order
rubrics_metrics.description: Disclosure and discovery activity are likely to involve confidential, proprietary, or private information warranting special protection from public disclosure and use other than prosecuting litigation. The Order does not confer blanket protections on all disclosures or responses and protection extends only to information entitled to confidential treatment under applicable legal principles. The Protective Order does not itself entitle parties to file confidential information under seal; Civil Local Rule 79-5 controls sealing procedures and standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — 'CONFIDENTIAL' Information or Items
rubrics_metrics.description: "CONFIDENTIAL" Information or Items: information (regardless of how it is generated, stored or maintained) or tangible things that qualify for protection under Federal Rule of Civil Procedure 26(c).

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — 'HIGHLY CONFIDENTIAL – ATTORNEYS' EYES ONLY'
rubrics_metrics.description: "HIGHLY CONFIDENTIAL – ATTORNEYS' EYES ONLY" Information or Items: extremely sensitive 'Confidential Information or Items,' disclosure of which to another Party or Non-Party would create a substantial risk of serious harm that could not be avoided by less restrictive means.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition — 'HIGHLY CONFIDENTIAL – SOURCE CODE'
rubrics_metrics.description: "HIGHLY CONFIDENTIAL – SOURCE CODE" Information or Items: extremely sensitive 'Confidential Information or Items' representing computer code and associated comments and revision histories, formulas, engineering specifications, or schematics that define or otherwise describe in detail the algorithms or structure of software or hardware designs, disclosure of which to another Party or Non-Party would create a substantial risk of serious harm that could not be avoided by less restrictive means.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of Protective Order Protections
rubrics_metrics.description: Protections cover protected material and (1) any information copied or extracted from Protected Material; (2) all copies, excerpts, summaries, or compilations of Protected Material; and (3) any testimony, conversations, or presentations by Parties or their Counsel that might reveal Protected Material.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Protections do not cover information in the public domain at time of disclosure or that becomes public by lawful means, nor information known to the Receiving Party prior to disclosure or obtained lawfully from a non-confidential source. Use of Protected Material at trial is governed by a separate agreement or order.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration of Confidentiality Obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: Even after final disposition of the litigation, the confidentiality obligations remain in effect until a Designating Party agrees otherwise in writing or a court order directs otherwise. Final disposition is dismissal of all claims/defenses or final judgment after completion of appeals, rehearings, remands, trials, or reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designating Protected Material — Exercise of Restraint and Care
rubrics_metrics.description: Each Party or Non-Party that designates information or items for protection must take care to limit any such designation to specific material that qualifies under appropriate standards. Mass, indiscriminate, or routinized designations are prohibited. Designations shown to be clearly unjustified or made for improper purpose expose the Designating Party to sanctions. If a designation is mistaken, the Designating Party must promptly notify others that it is withdrawing the mistaken designation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties should limit designations to specific qualifying portions and avoid over-broad claims of confidentiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designating Protected Material — Manner and Timing (Documentary Material)
rubrics_metrics.description: For documentary information (paper or electronic, excluding transcripts), the Producing Party must affix the legend 'CONFIDENTIAL,' 'HIGHLY CONFIDENTIAL – ATTORNEYS' EYES ONLY,' or 'HIGHLY CONFIDENTIAL – SOURCE CODE' to each page that contains protected material. If only portions of a page qualify, the Producing Party must clearly identify the protected portion(s) and specify the level of protection for each portion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Original documents made available for inspection need not be designated until after the inspecting Party indicates which material it wants copied and produced. During inspection and before designation, all material is deemed 'HIGHLY CONFIDENTIAL – ATTORNEYS' EYES ONLY' until produced and appropriately marked.
